author: Jamie Dimon
title: JPMorganChase 2025 Chairman and CEO Letter to Shareholders
headline: Jamie Dimon after a record year: war, deficits and high asset prices could bring stickier inflation and higher rates than markets expect.
summary: JPMorganChase earned a record $185.6 billion in revenue and $57.0 billion in net income in 2025, with a 20% return on tangible equity, and raised its dividend twice. Dimon sees a resilient US economy but warns that the war in Iran, oil shocks and reshaped supply chains may bring stickier inflation and higher rates than markets expect, while high asset prices leave little room for error. He holds about $40 billion of excess capital, calls bank stocks fully valued and expects losses on leveraged lending to surprise when the credit cycle turns. AI, in his view, is real and not a speculative bubble.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Raised the quarterly dividend from $1.25 to $1.40 and then to $1.50 per share; buybacks only keep excess capital from growing.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: About $40 billion of excess capital earns roughly 4% after tax today; Dimon expects to deploy it at excellent returns, which may take several years.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Many asset prices, bank stocks included, look fully valued. Household net worth is 560% of GDP, against a peak of 460% in 2006.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: Private credit: $1.8 trillion of leveraged loans with weaker covenants, more payment-in-kind interest and thin valuation marks. Losses should run higher than expected in the next credit cycle.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: AI spending by the five hyperscalers rises from $450 billion in 2025 to about $725 billion in 2026, probably inflationary in the short run.

risks.text: The wars in Iran and Ukraine: oil and commodity shocks could keep inflation sticky and push rates higher than markets expect.
US debt is forecast to rise from 100% to 120% of GDP by 2036; Dimon thinks it will probably be dealt with only in a crisis.
High asset prices and very low credit spreads mean that anything short of good outcomes could hit markets hard.

quotes.text: Overall, the investment in AI is not a speculative bubble; rather, it will deliver significant benefits.
the right way would be to deal with it now before it becomes a problem; the wrong way would be to let it become a crisis, which, in my opinion, is probably the likely outcome.
We have not had a credit recession in a long time, and it seems that some people assume it will never happen.

stocks.note: Record 2025; Dimon calls bank stocks fully valued and holds about $40 billion of excess capital.
